GitHub Copilot Instructions – sportyR

Source: .github/copilot-instructions.md

These instructions tell GitHub Copilot (and other AI coding assistants) how to write code that fits this repository. The fuller guide is CLAUDE.md; CONTRIBUTING.md covers the workflow.

sportyR draws scaled ggplot2 representations of sports playing surfaces (baseball, basketball, curling, football, hockey, lacrosse, soccer, softball, tennis, volleyball) from rule-book dimensions.

Golden rules

  1. Dimensions come from data-raw/surface-dimensions.json only. Never invent a measurement; rebuild R/sysdata.rda with data-raw/internal-datasets.R.
  2. Each sport is R/geom-<sport>.R (exported geom_<sport>()) plus R/features-<sport>.R (internal feature functions). Follow the existing sport’s shape; do not add a new abstraction.
  3. Never hand-edit NAMESPACE, man/, README.md or R/sysdata.rda. Edit roxygen / README.Rmd / the JSON and regenerate.
  4. Every test file starts with skip_on_cran(). CI sets NOT_CRAN: true.
  5. sportypy and sdvplot-js vendor surface-dimensions.json; a geometry change needs a re-vendor there.
  6. The CRAN maintainer submits to CRAN, not us. Never run submit_cran().
  7. Never add AI assistants as commit co-authors.

After changing code

  • devtools::document(), devtools::test(), devtools::check(args = "--as-cran").
  • Add new exported topics to _pkgdown.yml reference: (pkgdown::check_pkgdown()).
  • Update NEWS.md for user-visible changes; re-render README.Rmd if edited.
  • Commit with Conventional Commits (feat(softball):, fix(lacrosse):, …).
